newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Stocks to Watch Today - June 19.
newsitem.headline: Australian Stocks to Watch Today - June 19.

text.p: Some Australian stocks to watch this morning:

Investors are expected to applaud the proposed merger of Australian nickel producer QNI Ltd and the nickel interests of South Africa's Gencor Ltd when QNI shares are reinstated for trading on Thursday, stock brokers said on Wednesday. Brokers said the deal values QNI at between A$3.40 and A$3.50 a share, given a market value of A$2.3 billion based on the assets of the two groups and the financial clout on hand to possibly make acquisitions of low-cost operations.

BSkyB shares lost 770 million pounds ($1.3 billion) in value on Wednesday on a report the pay television company could be shut out of the bidding for new digital TV licences and the loss of key executives. The Financial Times said the Independent Television Commission (ITC) had told BSkyB it should drop its equity stake in a consortium with commercial TV groups Carlton and Granada, which has applied for digital terrestrial television (DTT) licences. The report said the consortium - British Digital Broadcasting - could be ruled out of the reckoning on competition grounds if BSkyB did not comply.

Molson Cos Ltd said on Wednesday that talks with Philip Morris Cos Inc unit Miller Brewing Co to buy out Miller's 20 percent stake in Molson Breweries were at an advanced stage. He said Molson's partnership agreement with Australian beermaker Foster's Brewing Group Ltd stipulated that Molson must share the purchase of Miller's stake with Foster's. Also Molson Breweries said on Wednesday that it will cut its price for beer in Canada's most populous province of Ontario by C$3.00 a case to C$26.15 for a case of 24 beers for two weeks starting June 30.
* Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd A$19.27 (-0.03)

Share analysts have revised up their profit forecasts for Australia's biggest company, The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd (BHP), after the embattled blue chip this week announced a strong rise in copper production. The revisions put the steel-making and resources giant on track for a slightly higher annual net profit of between A$1.35 billion and A$1.4 billion before abnormal items.

The Rundle twins said late on Wednesday they had acceptances from institutional investors for share issues raising a total of A$89.95 million. Southern Pacific Petroleum NL would issue 10.8 million shares at A$4.15 a share to raise A$44.82 million while Central Pacific Minerals NL would issue 4.75 million shares at A$9.50 a share to raise A$45.13 million, they said.
